newsitem.title: USA: Pet store workers take rabies shots, spare tiger.
newsitem.headline: Pet store workers take rabies shots, spare tiger.

text.p: Three pet store workers scratched by a rambunctious seven-month-old Bengal tiger have agreed to undergo a painful series of rabies shots to spare the tiger's life, the store manager said on Tuesday.
"It was either destroy the tiger or take the shots," Troy, a manager of the suburban Minneapolis Pet Smart store, said, asking that his full name not be used.

The tiger, named Elsa, weighs around 300 pounds (114 kg) and is one of two tigers owned by a rural Minnesota family. She became playful or frightened while having her photograph taken at the store on Saturday and scratched two of the workers and bit another. None were seriously hurt.

The three employees had in mind that Bengal tigers are an endangered species when they agreed to the series of six daily rabies shots. Animals that undergo tests for rabies must be destroyed, according to state law.
